record.original_question: For n simple closed curves in the plane, pairwise intersecting with no triple intersection points, determine the minimum possible number f(n) of intersection points; in particular, is lim_{n→∞} f(n)/binom(n,2) equal to 2?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.10 Find f (n). Is limn→∞ f (n)/ n2 = 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2 and consider families of n simple closed curves in the plane such that every two curves in the family intersect, and no three curves pass through a common point. Define f(n) to be the minimum, over all such families, of the total number of intersection points (counted as distinct points of the plane). 

(a) Determine f(n) exactly. 
(b) Decide whether lim_{n → ∞} f(n) / C(n,2) = 2, where C(n,2) = n(n-1)/2.
artifact.status_search_result: The asymptotic part (b) is settled: Pach, Rubin, and Tardos (SODA 2015 / CPC) proved the Richter–Thomassen conjecture, showing that any n pairwise intersecting simple closed curves in the plane, no three concurrent, determine at least (1 − o(1))n² intersection points, which together with the obvious upper bound 2·C(n,2) gives lim f(n)/C(n,2) = 2. The exact determination of f(n) for all n remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the Richter–Thomassen Conjecture about Pairwise Intersecting Closed Curves
status_evidence.snippet: Any n pairwise intersecting simple closed curves in the plane, no three of which pass through the same point, determine at least (1−o(1))n² intersection points.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic lower bound (1−o(1))n² is proved, establishing lim f(n)/C(n,2)=2.

status_evidence.title: Beyond the Richter-Thomassen Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Strengthens the Richter–Thomassen bound by showing crossings exceed touchings by a factor of Ω((log log n)^{1/8}).
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the asymptotic resolution while exact f(n) is not given.
